claims.text: Carbon-free CrNbTaTiW-based multilayer coatings deposited by room-temperature magnetron co-sputtering have a conventional columnar grain structure.
The carbon-free coating has relatively large, poorly stabilized grain boundaries.
Introducing 8 at.% carbon into selected layers produces a supersaturated solid solution.
At 8 at.% carbon, carbide precipitates can be avoided under the proposed processing and testing conditions.
Carbon incorporation refines the coating's grain structure.
Carbon incorporation stabilizes coherent grain boundaries.
The stabilized coherent grain boundaries are less susceptible to thermal fluctuations.
Carbon atoms segregate at grain boundaries.
Carbon-induced grain refinement and boundary stabilization impede grain-boundary sliding.
Carbon-induced grain refinement and boundary stabilization impede dislocation motion.
Impeded grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion reduce time-dependent plastic deformation.
Carbon-doped multilayers will exhibit significantly lower creep displacement than carbon-free multilayers at 573 K under identical static loading.
Carbon-doped multilayers will exhibit higher hardness than carbon-free multilayers.
The proposed mechanism applies near 573 K while carbon remains in a supersaturated solid solution.
Significantly higher temperatures may make the proposed mechanism ineffective.
Excessive carbon can cause carbide formation and thereby make the proposed mechanism ineffective.
The carbon-doped and carbon-free coatings should be compared under identical 573 K static-load conditions.
Failure to observe lower creep displacement, higher hardness, and refined grain boundaries in the carbon-doped coating would falsify the proposed hypothesis.
Detection of carbide formation in the carbon-doped coating would falsify the proposed supersaturated-solid-solution mechanism.
